purpose: Freeze a candidate-only M19 Teaching Assistant, Study Partner, and M20 handoff context for future human review without changing M19's legacy-baseline learner or release state.

truthBoundary.platform: This record neither controls nor verifies GPT Live quality, model selection, voice, microphone access, equation or code rendering, platform retention, or any external integration.
truthBoundary.records: This record defaults to learner-controlled local evidence and cannot itself write Notion notes, retain raw voice or transcripts, store credentials, or collect personal data.
truthBoundary.mastery: This candidate companion is not an oral-exam result, score, grade, publication, release, completion, or learner-mastery claim.

teachingAssistant.openingMove: Begin with one learner-selected concurrency claim. Ask which state is shared, who owns each transition, which progress guarantee is meant, and for the shortest interleaving before asking for a conclusion.
teachingAssistant.artifactFocus: Ask the learner to make one state invariant visible, reconstruct one labelled schedule or code trace, name one lost-update, visibility, deadlock, or cancellation boundary, and distinguish an observed run from the guarantees the design actually provides.
teachingAssistant.repairMove: Ask for a prediction before correction; change exactly one schedule, ownership rule, synchronization point, visibility assumption, cancellation point, or worker limit; then offer the smallest trace or counterexample without pass/fail framing.

studyPartner.rehearsalMove: Use the visible chat as a readable whiteboard: name the shared state and invariant, show a short labelled timeline or code trace, give a plain-language or ASCII fallback, and rehearse one history-to-guarantee-to-boundary chain at a time.
studyPartner.changedPremise: Change one interleaving, ownership boundary, synchronization primitive, visibility rule, cancellation event, or pool size. Ask for a prediction before looking at a schedule trace, counterexample, or progress argument.
studyPartner.taHandoff: End with the learner's selected concurrency card, attempted schedule or code trace, confidence, unresolved misconception, one scheduling or progress limitation, and a constructive focus for the Teaching Assistant's supportive oral defense.

forwardHandoff.carryArtifact: Carry a concurrent-history evidence card: shared state, owners, invariant, labelled schedule or trace, synchronization/progress assumptions, one failure boundary, and one uncertainty—not a mastery claim.
forwardHandoff.targetQuestion: Before treating a local send or completed request in M20 as a remote protocol effect, what message state, ownership boundary, ordering, retry, timeout, and durability assumption must become explicit?
forwardHandoff.boundary: M20 is the only canonical forward handoff. References to M21–M36 or M25/M26 are later conceptual connections, not learner-navigation bypasses, completion claims, or release evidence.
